answer.sourceLine: Sowell wrote it in his syndicated “Random thoughts on the passing scene” column. The Sun-Sentinel printed it on November 28, 1998. But the original says “a radical 50 years ago, a liberal 25 years ago,” not 60 and 30. The viral numbers are a later change to his wording.

source.excerpt: Random thoughts on the passing scene: … If you have always believed that everyone should play by the same rules and be judged by the same standards, that would have gotten you labeled a radical 50 years ago, a liberal 25 years ago and a racist today. A Washington Post writer declares, “the incomes of most American households have remained stubbornly flat over the past three decades.” Liberals have remained stubbornly blind to facts over the same period…
trail: Nov. 28, 1998. The sentence appears, with “50 years ago” and “25 years ago,” in Sowell’s Creators Syndicate “Random thoughts on the passing scene” column in the Sun-Sentinel ↗.
Wikiquote lists the 50/25 wording on its Thomas Sowell page ↗ and cites “Creators Syndicate, November 28, 1998.”
Dec. 27, 2016. A Townhall list published to mark Sowell’s retirement prints the altered numbers: “a radical 60 years ago, a liberal 30 years ago” (Townhall ↗).
Feb. 2021. WORLD’s review of a documentary about Sowell quotes the original 50/25 figures (WORLD ↗).
source.excerptNote: Transcribed from an Internet Archive copy of the Sun-Sentinel page. The headline was printed with the column there. The sentence is one item in a list of unrelated remarks.
source.rightsNote: The line comes from a newspaper column published in 1998, long after the 1931 cutoff, so it is still under copyright, held by Sowell and/or his syndicate (Creators Syndicate column, Nov. 28, 1998 ↗). Quoting one sentence with credit is ordinary commentary use.

misattribution.heading: Right author, wrong numbers
misattribution.intro: No one else is credited with this line, and it is genuinely Sowell’s. What drifted is the arithmetic. The most widely shared version changes his “50 years ago” and “25 years ago” to 60 and 30.

items.who: The “60 years ago … 30 years ago” version
items.why: This version appears, for example, in Townhall’s December 2016 list of Sowell quotes (Townhall ↗). Sowell’s 1998 column reads “a radical 50 years ago, a liberal 25 years ago” (Sun-Sentinel ↗). We found no Sowell source that uses 60 and 30. No source we found says who changed the figures.

misattribution.truthLine: Sowell wrote: “If you have always believed that everyone should play by the same rules and be judged by the same standards, that would have gotten you labeled a radical 50 years ago, a liberal 25 years ago and a racist today.” It comes from his Creators Syndicate column, as printed in the Sun-Sentinel, November 28, 1998 ↗.

context.heading: A one-liner in a list
lead: The sentence was not a speech or a book thesis. It is one entry in Sowell’s recurring “Random thoughts on the passing scene” column, a string of short, unrelated remarks. In the same 1998 column it sits between notes on late-talking children and household-income statistics. Nearby are quips about Bill Clinton, school choice and term limits.

Because the time spans are relative (“years ago”), the sentence is easy to “update” as it gets passed around. That may explain how 60 and 30 replaced 50 and 25, but this is our own observation; no source we found documents it. Anyone quoting Sowell exactly should use the 1998 figures.
detailsBody: We found no Quote Investigator article on this line; its Thomas Sowell tag ↗ lists two articles, both on other quotations.
Wikiquote lists the line under Sowell’s own quotations, with the 50/25 wording and a Creators Syndicate citation dated November 28, 1998 (Wikiquote ↗).
